title: Principles of Chemical Science
purpose: A complete ten-unit entry into university chemistry, connecting chemical bookkeeping and atomic structure to bonding, thermodynamics, equilibrium, kinetics, acid–base systems, electrochemistry, coordination chemistry and catalysis, with original problem sheets and a cumulative model-based capstone.
description:
Chemistry asks how the properties of matter follow from atoms, how atoms bond, which reactions are favoured and how fast they proceed. This course develops that chain through ten fully authored units: diagnostic chemical bookkeeping; atomic structure and periodicity; bonding and shape; thermodynamics and equilibrium; kinetics; acid–base systems; electrochemistry; coordination chemistry; catalysis; and a cumulative synthesis.

The primary study spine is MIT OpenCourseWare 5.111SC (Fall 2014, Catherine Drennan; CC BY-NC-SA 4.0). Exact lecture-note pages support the claims, while Corniversity supplies original explanations, exercises, progressive hints and instructor reasoning. OpenStax remains optional linked human reading only, under its recorded use restrictions; it was not read or imported for the 2026-11-12 completion. Source figures and problem sets are not copied.

Every unit has a lesson and assessed work. The final capstone connects atom/electron balance, molecular geometry, chemical equilibrium, pH, electrode potential, charge and energy, transition-metal models and experimental evidence. Calculations are virtual studies of stated models, not at-home laboratory instructions. Academic review status is recorded separately from structural availability; a prepared unit is not proof that a learner has mastered it.

Entry begins with the chemistry diagnostic. Mathematical experience alone does not establish chemistry readiness. Use attempts, feedback and revision to identify the bridge work you actually need.

outcomes.description: Use the mole, balanced equations, limiting reactants and molarity to convert between mass, amount, number of particles and concentration, with units, phases and assumptions stated.
outcomes.evidenceExpected: Diagnostic-unit exercises with unit-checked numeric answers, a mass-balance check and an explicit assumptions statement.

outcomes.description: Explain the quantum description of atoms (photons, hydrogen energy levels, orbitals, configurations of multi-electron atoms) and use it to predict and explain periodic trends.
outcomes.evidenceExpected: Photon and energy-level calculations, electron configurations of atoms and ions, and trend explanations that name the measurement (photoelectron spectroscopy) behind the data.

outcomes.description: Draw Lewis structures with formal charges and resonance, predict molecular shape and polarity with VSEPR, and use molecular-orbital bond orders for diatomics.
outcomes.evidenceExpected: Structures whose formal charges sum to the molecular charge, shape predictions with the AXE class named, and MO bond orders with magnetism explained.

outcomes.description: Compute ΔH°, ΔS°, ΔG° and K for reactions with standard states and temperature stated; predict the direction of change from Q versus K and the response to a stress.
outcomes.evidenceExpected: Thermochemical calculations by two routes with the discrepancy explained, an ICE-table equilibrium calculation and Le Châtelier predictions argued through Q and K.

outcomes.description: Determine rate laws from data, use integrated rate laws and half-lives, test a mechanism against a rate law, and relate forward and reverse rate constants to K in a reversible model.
outcomes.evidenceExpected: Kinetics exercises plus the virtual reversible-reaction model report with conservation law, solution, equilibrium and perturbation analysis.

outcomes.description: Separate a model's assumptions from the observations that test it, and say what measurement would distinguish two candidate explanations.
outcomes.evidenceExpected: Written explanations and the laboratory interpretation that state assumptions (temperature, pressure, phase, standard state, ideality) and name a distinguishing observation.

outcomes.description: Solve acid–base, buffer, titration and coupled-speciation problems with mass/charge balances and checked approximations.
outcomes.evidenceExpected: Unit6 problem sheet and unit10 speciation/capstone calculations with explicit equilibrium and reservoir assumptions.

outcomes.description: Balance redox reactions and connect cell potential, reaction free energy, activities, charge and useful product amount.
outcomes.evidenceExpected: Unit7 sheet and cumulative capstone with Nernst, Faraday and energy accounting and independently testable efficiency claims.

outcomes.description: Use coordination, electron-count and crystal-field models to interpret geometry, magnetic and spectral evidence while stating their limits.
outcomes.evidenceExpected: Unit8 structural-inference sheet and capstone model comparison supported by multiple observations.

outcomes.description: Derive a simple enzyme rate law and distinguish catalytic rate effects, equilibrium, identifiability and experimental evidence.
outcomes.evidenceExpected: Unit9 derivations/transfer and unit10 controlled-experiment synthesis with alternative mechanisms and falsifiable predictions.

assessmentSpecs.title: Diagnostic entry check
assessmentSpecs.description: The three unit 1 exercises, submitted as immutable attempts. They establish readiness evidence for the course's entry rule; a failed first attempt routes to the matching reading and a second attempt, not to a grade.

assessmentSpecs.title: Problem sets
assessmentSpecs.description: Each prepared unit's exercises, assessed with first-gap localisation. Chemistry answers must respect stoichiometry, charge and unit constraints and state temperature, pressure, phase and standard-state assumptions. Revision is expected; the portfolio of attempts is the record.
rubricSummary: units, significant figures and sign conventions

assessmentSpecs.title: Virtual kinetics model report
assessmentSpecs.description: The reversible first-order model A ⇌ B at constant volume (unit 5): derive the conservation law and the solution, compute the equilibrium composition and relaxation time, analyse what changes when a rate constant doubles, and say which observation distinguishes equilibrium from no reaction. A virtual activity on a stated model, never an at-home experiment.

assessmentSpecs.title: Synthesis: equilibrium from both sides
assessmentSpecs.description: Unit10 cumulative problem sheet and carbon-conversion capstone: reconcile equilibrium and rates; preserve mass/charge and standard states; integrate bonding, acid speciation, electrochemistry, coordination models and a controlled evidence plan. Open book; estimates support planning rather than a forced time limit.
rubricSummary: charge, amount and energy with units

externalSyllabusNote: Adapted study path using MIT OpenCourseWare 5.111SC Principles of Chemical Science (Fall 2014) materials under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, with OpenStax Chemistry 2e section pages as linked reading. The original course ran 35 lectures in five units over one MIT term with nine problem sets, four exams and clicker participation, and assumed one year of high-school chemistry with no formal prerequisites. Corniversity re-paces it as 10 units, replaces the commercial textbook with OpenStax sections, and sets its own exercises, a virtual kinetics model and a written synthesis. This is not an MIT course and confers no credit anywhere.
